title: Financial Reports for the owners
changes: Owners now have a Financial Reports page under Admin with the accountant's monthly reports from June 2024 to May 2026 in one place.
See profit and loss month by month, each shop's results, the balance sheet, cash, targets against actual, and the top products, customers and suppliers.
When the accountant corrects an earlier month in a later report, the page shows the corrected figure. Only the three owners can open it.

title: Black Friday forecast
changes: For Black Friday, Mohammed now shows what you can realistically expect to sell next to the most you could sell, as a low, likely and high range.
The forecast comes from each product's recent sales and how the shop sold in past Black Friday weeks. Products with no recent sales are not counted on.
Plans are ranked by the profit you can expect, so the products most likely to pay off come first.

title: Mohammed plans whole campaigns
changes: Ask Mohammed for any campaign (Black Friday, Ramadan, National Day) and he builds it in three groups: popular pieces to bring customers in, profitable offers customers want, and selected slow stock.
Each product shows its price, cost, stock, recent sales, the offer, the profit after it, and why customers would want it, ranked by what it brings the campaign.
Before suggesting a large discount on an expensive watch, he compares it with smaller offers and explains what it would gain.

title: Mohammed thinks like a watch retailer
changes: Mohammed protects brand value: he starts with the smallest offer that would be noticed, keeps deep public discounts for pieces that truly have not sold, and suggests private offers for premium watches.
Gifts now match the watch, such as a Gerald Charles strap with a Gerald Charles watch. He no longer suggests a token gift on an expensive piece.
Offer plans show each product on its own line with the old price, new price, offer, stock and profit, then list what he left out and why.
Plan totals are shown as the most you could make if everything sells, kept apart from what to actually expect.

title: Mohammed gives advice
changes: Ask Mohammed now answers like a business partner: the decision first, the key numbers in a short table, then exactly what to do.
Ask him for an offer plan (Black Friday, a sale, clearing slow stock) and he picks real products, sets the discount or gift on each and shows the profit after the offer.
Follow-ups change the last plan instead of starting again: "less discount", "gifts instead", "only Hoffman".
Every answer has a Copy button that copies clean text ready for WhatsApp or email.

title: Shop costs
changes: Payroll now shows each shop's month next to its rent and its staff's pay, with what is left of its sales before the cost of goods. Online and WhatsApp sales count with the head office.
Tap a shop's rent to change it from a given month; the earlier rents stay listed.

title: Payroll
changes: A new Payroll page for the owners: each person's salary and allowances, every increment with its date, bonuses and deductions, and the month's total to pay.
Commission is worked out from Lightspeed: 2.5% once Avenues reaches 45,000 KD or Time Gallery 10,000 KD in the month, on each salesperson's own sales.
Approve a month to lock it, then mark it as paid.

title: Logos on the new boutiques
changes: Five of the Promenade's new boutiques carry their brand's own logo: Beda’a, Wolf, Baltic, Citizen and Seven Friday. Raketa keeps its painted name for now.

title: The Promenade
changes: Time Keeper World's mall has a new section, The Promenade, with six boutiques: every brand with more than 5,000 KD of stock at cost now has its own shop. Beda’a, Wolf, Baltic, Citizen, Raketa and Seven Friday moved in.
West End's sign shows the brand's own W emblem with its name beside it, so it reads at a glance.
In the Loading Dock, an owner can set the date an order is expected to arrive, with a note. Lightspeed's own due date stays as it is, and an order past the owners' date is marked to review.

title: A quicker start, and the right numbers
changes: The app opens faster: it downloads less before the first screen appears, and each page arrives the first time you open it.
The dashboard, the Inbox and the Stock page load their figures faster.
The dashboard's supplier balance, open purchase orders, shipments and brand chart now count every purchase order. They were reading only about half.
Birthday and occasion reminders now cover every customer with a date, not only the first thousand customers.
A screen left open past midnight keeps updating by itself.

title: A new Loading Dock
changes: The Loading Dock in Time Keeper World is rebuilt: one bay per supplier with open orders, the largest amount still to come first, each with a small number tag. Tap a bay to see the supplier's orders.
Each order shows what is still to come and how much has arrived, with three small icons for the order, the shipment and the payment. Tap an icon to see what it means.
An order opens on Items, Receiving and Payment tabs. Anything worth checking sits in one short "to review" row: tap a point to see why.
Receiving and Payments have their own corners of the dock, and the bar at the bottom takes you to open orders, partly received orders and payments.
Lightspeed's order status is shown exactly as Lightspeed has it, and an order is never called late unless an expected date is on record.
The seven boutiques in the Watch Mall now carry their brands' own logos on signs fixed to their shop fronts, sized so the name reads without covering the shop.

title: Time Keeper World, for owners
changes: Owners have a new Time Keeper World: tap World at the top of the screen, beside the bell. The shop floor, the loading dock and the office are drawn as one place you can look around.
The floor is the Watch Mall. Every brand has its own boutique or display case, showing how its stock is selling; tap it for units, cost, sales, open orders and what to do next.
Find any brand by name, or jump straight to the Grand Gallery, Collectors' Arcade or Discovery Court.
Brands stay where an owner puts them. Owners can move a brand, feature it or give its boutique a colour, and every change is recorded.
Only the owners can open it. Nobody else sees the World button, and the World is never downloaded to their phones.
On Today, a sales channel with no target (such as WhatsApp) no longer says "no target" twice.

title: Marketing campaigns
changes: Owners can turn a marketing idea into a campaign from the Inbox: pick the goal, the watches, a target and a deadline, and give it to the marketing team.
The marketing team gets each campaign as a task in their Inbox. Open it to see the brief, upload drafts and send them for review.
The owner sees the draft pictures, approves them or asks for changes, and gets a message when a draft is waiting.
Once a post is out, the team records when it went out and the link. Nothing is posted, boosted or paid for from the app.
Every step is kept in the campaign's history, with a lesson at the end, so you can see what worked.

title: A new face for Mohammed
changes: Ask Mohammed has a new drawn portrait that is easier to make out at small size.

title: Ask Mohammed
changes: Ask is now “Ask Mohammed”: a face in the corner of every page. Tap it to ask about stock, sales or what to buy, then close it and carry on.
The conversation stays while you move between pages, and starts fresh the next time you open the app.
The separate Ask page is gone from the menu.

title: Ask starts fresh
changes: Opening Ask now starts a new, empty conversation instead of showing the last one.

title: Ask: questions about stock and sales
changes: Owners have a new Ask page. Ask in English or Arabic about stock, sales, brands, or what to buy or reorder, and get an answer from Lightspeed's figures.
Every answer shows the period it covers, when stock and sales were last updated, and anything estimated or missing.
Follow-up questions keep the brand, product and period, so there's no need to repeat them.
Tap thumbs up or down on an answer to say whether it was right, and what was wrong.

title: Clock-ins not closed, person by person
changes: Tapping the “clock-ins never closed” alert now opens a list: one card per person with each day, the time they came in and where.
Each card has a ready message for that person (Arabic or English) to send on WhatsApp or copy, telling them which days to correct.
Alerts that open a page (attendance, purchase orders, projects) now land on that page when the app was closed, instead of the home page.

title: One alert, one app
changes: If you also use the shop app (DSR), alerts no longer arrive twice. Purchase orders, projects, tasks, accounts and marketing alerts come here; requests, birthdays and shop alerts go to the shop app.

title: Arabic names for WhatsApp messages
changes: HR → Employees has a new “Name in Arabic” field. Arabic WhatsApp messages are signed with it.
Arabic WhatsApp messages are rewritten to read naturally, name the shop in Arabic, and say “الساعة” when no product is named.

title: Customers: focus on the ones that matter
changes: Customers now opens on Top: customers who spent 1,000 KD or more, or bought 3+ times, and were seen in the last year (sorted by what they spent).
New filters: Win back (top customers not seen for a year), and New (first purchase in the last 60 days). Each shows how many.
Searching still looks through all customers, whichever filter is open.
Each customer shows a Top, Win back or New tag. The VIP filter is replaced by Top.

title: All customers now searchable
changes: Customers: the list now loads every customer instead of the first 1,000, so searches find everyone and the Occasions filter shows the customers it counts.

title: A dashboard for the manager
changes: The Dashboard is now built for the manager who runs the day: what needs fixing today, not how the company is doing.
Staffing shows who is not in yet, outlet by outlet. When everyone is in, it is one quiet line.
Each outlet’s sales sit against its target with a mark for where it should be today, so the outlet falling behind stands out.
“Waiting on you” puts approvals, overdue repairs, arrived pre-orders and follow-ups in one list, oldest first.
Watch shows lost sales, what customers asked for that we did not have, and late deliveries.
Supplier balance, stock value, ads and Instagram move to a new “Owner view” in the menu (owner only).

title: One PO notification a day
changes: Purchase-order updates now arrive as one summary at 9:00 each morning instead of one notification per change.

title: Manager approval shown
changes: Requests waiting for you now show which manager approved them and when, with their remarks.

title: Proposals show their post
changes: Each campaign proposal now shows its Instagram post on the card, with Open post to boost it straight from Instagram.

title: Media & Marketing, simpler
changes: Media & Marketing now has five pages: Marketing Overview, Ads, Client Ads, Instagram and Influencers.
Ads: Meta campaigns and campaign proposals are now two tabs on one page, with a count of proposals waiting for you.
The campaign list is shorter: one line for Meta’s health and three figures at the top.
Client Ads replaces Paid Ads Tracker: what clients booked, what they still owe, and which reports are due.
Link a client job to its Instagram post and its reach and views fill in by themselves. “Copy report for client” copies them ready to send.
Old links and bookmarks still work and open the new pages.

title: Marketing Overview
changes: New first page in Media & Marketing: Marketing Overview replaces Growth Review.
See at a glance what needs you: tracking, when ads last ran, proposals to decide, and money clients still owe.
Four figures against last week, and a chart of ad spend next to online sales, day by day.
“What we’re pushing”: ad money per brand next to that brand’s sales, where the ads send people, and which page ran them.
Brands are now recognised in Arabic captions too, so far fewer campaigns show as unknown. “Needs a brand” lists only the ones left.
Paid Ads Tracker is no longer shown to sales staff.

title: Media & Marketing fixes
changes: Content Planner is hidden from the menu for now; nothing in it was deleted.
Instagram keeps showing the latest followers after its first year, and Sync now says when the Instagram part fails.
Posted or finished items no longer show as Overdue.
Meta Campaigns: the Paid Ads Tracker link works, refresh errors are shown, and “Needs a brand” stays filtered while you search.
Growth Review: tap a campaign to open it; Try again if the review fails to load.
Campaign Proposals: withdrawing is recorded, Approve asks “are you sure?” first, and a build that stopped halfway can be approved again.
Influencers: one Status filter instead of two, no more 0.0× return when no revenue is entered, and followers typed on the list feed the growth chart.

title: What's new opens properly on phones
changes: Tapping the version at the top of the screen now opens What's new over the whole screen, instead of showing only its title.

title: Less reading in Media & Marketing
changes: Meta Campaigns, Growth Review, Instagram and Campaign Proposals say the same things in far fewer words.

title: Shorter campaign proposals
changes: Each proposal now shows just the goal, budget and target. Tap Details for the audience, post and reasons.

title: Growth Review fits the phone
changes: The Weekly Growth Review no longer slides sideways on a phone; long product names are shortened to fit.
Best-selling products now list only real products — charges such as delivery no longer appear as a nameless product.

title: Campaign checks that tell you what to do
changes: “Ask Meta to check” now tries the whole campaign on Meta and removes it again, so it catches problems the old check missed. Nothing is left behind and nothing spends.
When Meta can’t build a campaign yet, the proposal says what to do instead, such as boosting the post from the Instagram app.

title: Clearer when Meta says no
changes: When Meta refuses a campaign, the proposal now says in plain words what an owner needs to do, and shows the refusal once instead of twice.

title: Marketing you can act on
changes: Growth Review: each week's spend, sales, return on spend and cost per purchase, the best product and creative, and a Scale / Hold / Improve / Stop call for every campaign. It also arrives as a notification on Sunday morning.

Campaign Proposals: propose a campaign with its product, goal, audience, Instagram post, budget, reason and success measure. An owner approves it, it is built on Meta paused, and it spends only when an owner switches it on.
Meta Campaigns now shows purchase value, return on spend and cost per purchase, a daily check of whether website purchases are reaching Meta, Meta's time zone, and where the KD rate comes from.
Instagram Performance now shows Instagram's own figures: reach, profile visits, website taps, and each post's reach, saves, shares and views.
The KD rate for ad spend now updates every morning. An owner can still pin one in Settings.

title: Attendance follows the person, not the spelling
changes: Renaming someone in HR no longer detaches their past attendance: lateness is judged against their own shift, and they are counted once in Present today.

title: Hours no longer counted twice
changes: If a clock-in goes through twice, the portal no longer adds the same hours twice; a second clock-in while you are already clocked in is now refused.

title: First numbered release
changes: Requests: leave, corrections and schedule changes in one Inbox, with reminders.
Leave goes to the store manager first, then to the owners.
An attendance correction asks for the actual times, and approving it fixes the record.
HR can change someone's working days and hours from the Employees page.
Lateness is judged against each person's own hours, with grace set per shift.
Clock in at whichever workplace you are standing in. Clocking out works without location.
Sales by shop come from the tills. The Time Keeper register is split into Online and WhatsApp.
Meta ads: spend in dinars, and what each campaign bought for which brand.
CRM: each customer's visits and Lightspeed purchases on one page, shown only to those allowed.
Send WhatsApp from the CRM and the follow-up board, with English or Arabic templates.
Birthday and anniversary reminders go to the right salesperson.
Fixed: the app going white on iPhone Safari.
The version and build now show in the app. Tap them to see this list.
